title: Best CapEx Planning Software in 2026: 7 Platforms Compared for Project Phasing and Reallocation Governance
summary: Compare 7 CapEx planning platforms on project phasing, approval routing and reallocation governance, with a comparison table and buyer FAQs.
body_markdown:
*Last updated: November 2026*


**Key takeaways**


-


The best CapEx planning software lets finance phase projects, route approvals by amount and role, and govern every in-year reallocation with a record of who approved what and why.


-


Spreadsheet trackers can't tie spend back to an approval. A governed plan can.


-


Compare platforms on approval depth, project phasing, reallocation controls, ERP connections and who owns the model after go-live.


-


Capital and operating budgets belong in one plan, so approved capital stays visible next to the P&L.


## Introduction


The seven CapEx planning platforms worth comparing in 2026 are Abacum, Anaplan, Oracle Cloud EPM Planning, Workday Adaptive Planning, Planful, Pigment and Finario. They range from dedicated capital project systems to broader planning platforms with capital planning built in or built on top.


Abacum is the AI-native FP&A platform finance trusts, and the business planning platform the whole company runs on. It runs on one governed layer of data, logic and context: data is the what, logic is the how, context is the why.


Capital spend is lumpy, long-lived and hard to reverse. That makes the in-year moments, when a project overruns, a priority shifts or funds move between projects, the moments that need the most control. This guide compares the platforms through the lens of project phasing and reallocation governance.


## What is reallocation governance in CapEx planning?


Reallocation governance is the set of policies, approvals and records that decide how approved capital can move between projects, phases or categories after the budget is set. It keeps every move documented, approved by the right person and auditable.


Project phasing adds a second layer. Capital projects rarely run as one expense. They move through stages such as design, procurement, installation and commissioning, each with its own amount, timeline and approval. Good software tracks spend against each phase and enforces control when money needs to move between them. For background on the accounting basics, see our glossary entry on[capital expenditures (CapEx)](https://www.abacum.ai/glossary/capital-expenditures-capex) .


## What to look for in CapEx planning software


### Can you route approvals by amount, role and project type?


Look for approval tiers tied to your delegation of authority. A small adjustment should not need the same sign-off as a cross-project move, and the platform should show who approved each step.


### Can you phase projects across stages and periods?


Each phase should have its own authorized amount, spend curve and milestone, so variance on one phase triggers a review before the next tranche is released.


### How are reallocations controlled?


Ask what happens when a project exceeds its approved amount or when funds move between projects. You want triggers, a documented rationale, an approver and an updated view of project economics.


### Do capital and operating budgets live in one plan?


Capital decisions change depreciation, cash and operating costs. When capital sits in a separate tool, someone has to reconcile it by hand.


### Who maintains the model?


Ask who builds the capital model, who changes it when policy changes and what that costs in time and outside help.


## 7 CapEx planning software platforms compared


### 1. Abacum


**Best for:** Finance teams that want capital budgets planned, approved and tracked in the same governed plan as the P&L and operating budgets.


We built Abacum as the AI-native business planning platform for scaling enterprises. Capital and operating budgets live in one governed plan, so every team works from the same numbers. Budget owners build their own budgets in dedicated Spaces with controlled access. Submissions move through statuses (in progress, submitted, approved), permissions change by stage, and once a budget is approved the budget owner loses edit access, so finance owns the final number. Every change is tracked in an audit trail.


Allocation and phasing logic lives in driver-based rules, so you can structure each project as its own line or set of phase lines with an authorized amount and a spend curve. In a demo, we will show how your project and phase structure would be modeled. Weekly planning and reporting granularity means you can compare capital actuals to plan every week, and AI-generated variance commentary flows into narrative reporting and the board pack, grounded in the governed financial model.


AI Modeler changes who can keep a model current. Describe what you need in plain language, or start from the spreadsheet you already built, and get a working model in minutes. Add a product line, a section or new variables by asking, even in models you inherited. Every model explains itself, so you can ask what drives any line before the board meeting. AI Modeler proposes the plan, our calculation engine performs every calculation, and nothing saves until you approve it. It is included with the platform, with no credits, no meter and no hidden fees.


85% of our customers use AI in Abacum every month (Abacum customer usage data, October 2026). Actuals arrive through native, automated connections to your ERP and source systems, part of 700+ integrations, and multi-entity roll-ups apply FX translation at the rates you set. Most teams go live in six to nine weeks, depending on data complexity, entity count and workflows.


### 2. Anaplan


**Best for:** Planning programs with dedicated model builders.


Anaplan is a long-standing connected planning platform with multi-dimensional modeling and a large template ecosystem, and it publishes dedicated CapEx planning solution pages. It supports intricate model designs and large data volumes. The depth comes with a steeper setup and administration curve, so confirm who will build and maintain the capital model after go-live.


### 3. Oracle Cloud EPM Planning


**Best for:** Organizations already invested in the Oracle ecosystem that want module-based planning.


Oracle's documentation describes module-based planning for Financials, Workforce, Capital, Projects and Strategic Modeling. The Capital module supports requesting, justifying, reviewing and approving capital expense plans, with driver-based calculations of the effect on profit, cash flow and funding. The Projects module links project planning to the financial plan. Review the configuration effort and which modules you would enable.


### 4. Workday Adaptive Planning


**Best for:** Teams already on Workday that want capital planning connected to their financial and workforce plans.


Workday Adaptive Planning includes a capital sheet template where users pick an asset class, enter cost and units, and the sheet applies depreciation timing automatically. For request and approval workflows, Workday also offers a Capital Project Planning application built on Workday Extend that complements Adaptive Planning and requires an Extend subscription. Confirm which components your use case needs.


### 5. Planful


**Best for:** Finance teams that want a structured, process-driven platform with capital planning alongside budgeting and reporting.


Planful lists out-of-the-box CapEx and workforce planning in its financial planning features, along with audit trails and an Excel-like formula experience. It supports multi-entity roll-ups and structured planning cycles. Implementation involves structured configuration work and benefits from defined internal ownership.


### 6. Pigment


**Best for:** Teams willing to design and maintain their own capital planning model.


Pigment is a flexible modeling platform for teams willing to build and maintain their own planning models. Your team or an implementation partner designs it and keeps it running, so confirm who will own the model after go-live. Capital plans are a use case you design in the model, so ask to see a reference build for phasing and approvals.


### 7. Finario


**Best for:** Enterprises that want a dedicated system of record for a large capital project portfolio.


Finario describes its product as capital planning software purpose-built for enterprise CapEx portfolios. Its materials highlight rules-based approval routing by spend level, project type, asset class and business unit, stage gates from feasibility through post-completion review, re-approval when overrun thresholds are breached, and actuals tracking from the ERP. Because it focuses on capital, check how it connects to your operating plan and P&L.

## How to choose the right CapEx platform


1.


**Map your approval policy first.** List amount bands, roles and triggers, then test each platform against them.


2.


**Decide where capital should live.** If you want capital next to the P&L and operating budgets, favor a platform that holds both in one plan.


3.


**Test a reallocation end to end.** Ask each vendor to walk through an overrun, from trigger to approval to updated forecast.


4.


**Check ownership.** If every policy change needs a partner, in-year control will lag the business.


5.


**Spreadsheet-first teams should start with Abacum.** Our Excel Connector lets you import a budget or forecast as a version and export work to Excel and Google Sheets.
